title: The residue translation functors give the integrable Fock-space action
statement: Assume AC. The exact residue functors on genuine finite-n parabolic blocks have multiplicity-free generalized-standard flags given by valid single-entry moves $i\to i+1$ and $i+1\to i$. Their K0 operators are the full integrable $gl_{I^+}$ Fock Chevalley action, satisfying the integral Chevalley/Serre relations on the standard basis. For each simple, a residue translate vanishes exactly when its corresponding crystal edge is absent; otherwise it is a self-dual indecomposable with simple equal head/socle $L(\tilde f_iA)$ or $L(\tilde e_iA)$. The full tensor Fock module is represented by all standard classes; the ground-state class, with $M(A_\Lambda)=L(A_\Lambda)=P(A_\Lambda)$, generates only its multiplicity-one highest constituent. No action on labels alone proves the K0 relations or head/socle statement.
strategy: The earlier Casimir supplier proves actual flags, the standard-class isomorphism, relations and local integrability BEFORE the head lemma, so there is no circular dependence on this combined theorem. The local affine-Hecke helper proves the complete categorical extremal-string/simple-socle argument and matches labels by the actually read source-upper Chevalley leading-term proof. Apply it with E=f_i,F=e_i (and the swapped root orientation), then use restricted duality. For the ground multiset the column-strict admitted label is unique: successive strict entries at least their row ground values, with that minimal total weight forcing equality. The15 highest-weight/character bases therefore make its standard simple and projective. All quantum global/form claims have their own explicit later dictionary; this is the ungraded categorical result.
